claims.text: High-throughput computational screening using ab initio calculations can be used to assess phase stability in crystalline materials.
High-throughput computational screening using ab initio calculations can be used for microstructure refinement in crystalline materials.
High-throughput computational screening using ab initio calculations can be used for property optimization in crystalline materials.
The proposed method applies to crystalline structures with variable composition and microstructure.
The proposed screening can address operating conditions including temperature and pressure.
Electronic structure and atomic arrangement are the structural mediators connecting the computational intervention to the predicted results.
Ab initio calculations model the electronic structure of crystalline materials.
Ab initio calculations model the atomic arrangement of crystalline materials.
Modeling electronic structure and atomic arrangement enables prediction of phase stability.
Modeling electronic structure and atomic arrangement enables prediction of microstructure refinement.
Modeling electronic structure and atomic arrangement enables property optimization.
The proposed method will improve phase stability by 20% relative to traditional processing methods.
The proposed method will refine microstructure by 15% relative to traditional processing methods.
The proposed method will optimize properties by 10% relative to traditional processing methods.
The effectiveness of the proposed method is limited by available computational resources.
The effectiveness and reliability of the proposed method are limited by the accuracy of ab initio calculations.
The complexity of crystalline materials limits confidence in the proposed predictions.
The hypothesis is to be falsified if improvements in phase stability, microstructure refinement, and property optimization are less than 5% relative to traditional processing methods.
